text.p: The Australian bond market underperformed against the dollar bloc for the second successive session as it took a cautious view ahead of Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls report.
The dilemma for the market is Monday's local holiday, meaning that it will have to wait until Tuesday before it can reposition itself, analysts said.
"Basically, the market is going to have be as flat as it can be in the interim period, and that is putting us under some selling pressure," one trader said.

However, as the local market remains primed for a further monetary policy easing by the Reserve Bank, the Federal Reserve has tightening bias, and traders expect domestic bonds to outperform the U.S. in the short-term.
Some analysts are looking for a break of key resistance at 65 basis points on the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond spread to open up the way to 50 b.p..
